newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia cuts may not help total budget-Bank.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia cuts may not help total budget-Bank.

text.p: The federal government's budget cuts may have little impact on reducing Australia's total budget deficit because Australia's states appear to have loosened their belts, according to BankSA's November Trends bulletin.

"Even assuming the federal government succeeds in its aim of reducing its own deficit by A$4.7 billion, it now seems likely that, after allowance for the states, the improvement in the overall public sector underlying deficit may be as little as A$1.3 billion," it said.
"That suggests that, despite all the fuss about the budget cuts, they may have little impact," it said.
"Or in other words, there has been much ado about nothing - at least nothing much," the report said.

Part of the blame could be cast on the federal government because of the cutback in state grants, but most lay with budgeted increases in spending by the states, notably Queensland, Victoria and New South Wales, BankSA said.

It said analysis of federal own-purpose spending and unemployment rates suggested the long-term success or failure of the 1996/97 budget's attempt to wind back federal spending also would rest heavily on the fate of the unemployed.
"So far in 1996/97 the news on that front has been modest," the report said.
"Current unemployment rates are higher than those at the start of this financial year and also higher than the government's budget-time prediction for June 1997 of 8.25 percent," it said.
